explanation: Ariadne, daughter of King Minos, gave Theseus a ball of thread to find his way out. The Minotaur, half man and half bull, was her half-brother.

claims.text: In Greek myth, Theseus killed the Minotaur in the Labyrinth on Crete.
Perseus, Heracles and Jason did not kill the Minotaur.
Ariadne, daughter of King Minos of Crete, gave Theseus a ball of thread so he could find his way out of the Labyrinth.
The Minotaur, half man and half bull, was born to Minos's wife Pasiphaë, Ariadne's mother, which made it Ariadne's half-brother.

evidence.restatement: Theseus of Athens killed the Minotaur inside Minos's Labyrinth on Crete.
Perseus killed Medusa, Heracles is known for his Labours and Jason for the Golden Fleece; none of them killed the Minotaur.
Ariadne, daughter of Minos, gave Theseus a ball of thread so he could retrace his path out of the Labyrinth.
The Minotaur was Pasiphaë's son by the Cretan bull and Ariadne was Pasiphaë's daughter by Minos, so they were half-siblings.

evidence.restatement: Perseus beheaded Medusa, Jason led the Argonauts, and Heracles captured the Cretan Bull (the Minotaur's father in some tellings); none of them killed the Minotaur.
Ariadne, a daughter of King Minos, gave Theseus the ball of thread that let him find his way out of the Labyrinth.
The Minotaur was born to Minos's wife Pasiphaë after her union with a bull, and in the usual tradition Pasiphaë was also Ariadne's mother, so the two were half-siblings.
